Answer: B
Reason: Comparison of the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right middle/lower lung zone, with the follow-up X-ray (Figure 4) reveals that the original right-sided opacity has increased in extent and new patchy opacities have appeared in the left lung. This pattern of progressive, multifocal airspace disease is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma), which can present with pneumonic-type consolidation that spreads over time.
